title: Someone dared the punishment to come.
subtitle: Mocking a warning instead of heeding it
then: In Makkah the deniers laughed at the warning of the Last Day. Some went as far as praying: {trap}if this is the truth, rain stones down on us.{/trap} The surah opens by naming that dare and answering it: {idea}the punishment is real and on its way.{/idea}
now: Someone at work jokes, "If God cared, He would have done something by now." Or you catch yourself thinking a warning does not apply since nothing has happened yet. {trap}Silence is not the same as safety.{/trap}
old: If nothing bad has happened yet, the warning was probably exaggerated.
new: A delay is not a denial. What is promised is already on its way.
try: Think of one warning you have been brushing off. Take it seriously for five minutes today.

title: When it comes, nobody can push it back.
subtitle: No one stands between the denier and the Day
then: The deniers of Quraysh trusted their clans and their wealth to protect them from anything. Ibn Kathir explains the verse plainly: {trap}no one can repel it if Allah wants it to happen.{/trap} The usual shields of Makkah would not work here.
now: You know how to get out of most things: a phone call, a favour, a good lawyer, the right excuse. That skill makes you feel untouchable. {idea}Some doors cannot be talked open.{/idea} The time to prepare is before you reach them.
old: There is always someone who can get me out of trouble.
new: Before Allah's decree, my connections and excuses carry no weight.
try: Notice one area where you rely on talking your way out. Choose honesty there today.

title: It comes from the Lord of the ways up.
subtitle: Who stands behind the warning

row.title: Allah
sub: owner of the ways of ascent

then: The deniers spoke as if the warning were just Muhammad's ﷺ idea. This verse names the source. Ibn Abbas said the ways of ascent mean {idea}loftiness and abundance{/idea}, and Mujahid said they are {idea}the ways of rising into the heavens.{/idea}
now: A notice from a friend you can ignore. A letter from the court you cannot. You open it differently because of who sent it. {idea}The Quran is a message from the One above everything{/idea}, and it reads differently when you remember that.
old: A reminder is only as serious as the person reading it to me.
new: The weight of the message comes from the One who sent it.
try: Before you read Quran next, pause and say: this is from my Lord. Then read.

title: A Day as long as fifty thousand years.
subtitle: The length of the Day of Judgement

sub: years, the measure of that Day

row.title: endless
sub: for those who withheld and denied

then: Ibn Abbas and others said this Day is the Day of Judgement. Ibn Kathir cites a hadith about the wealthy who {trap}did not give the due on their wealth{/trap}, standing through a Day of fifty thousand years until judgement is passed. The length is felt by those who denied.
now: A five-minute wait at the doctor's feels like an hour when you are scared. A long dinner with friends flies by. {idea}Time stretches with how you arrive.{/idea} What you do with your wealth and hours now shapes how long that Day will feel.
old: Judgement is one quick moment at the end.
new: That Day is long, and how it feels depends on what I bring to it.
try: Give something small today from what you have, even if no one asks.

title: Be patient, and make it beautiful.
subtitle: Patience without bitterness while being mocked
then: Ibn Kathir says this was addressed to the Prophet ﷺ: {idea}be patient with your people's rejection{/idea} and with their demand to hurry the punishment, since they thought it would never come. He was not told to argue harder. He was told to wait well.
now: A relative keeps mocking your prayer at family dinners. A colleague rolls their eyes every time you decline the drinks. You can stay quiet and stew, or you can stay kind. {idea}Beautiful patience keeps your heart clean while you wait.{/idea}
old: Being patient means swallowing it and resenting them quietly.
new: Real patience is calm and trusting, with no grudge hidden inside it.
try: The next time someone needles you today, answer once, kindly, and let it go.

title: They see it as far away.
subtitle: The comfort of thinking the end is distant
then: Ibn Kathir explains that the word for far, {trap}ba'id{/trap}, here means something they thought impossible. The deniers of Makkah did not just think the Hour was late. {trap}They thought it would never come.{/trap}
now: You plan to fix your prayer when life calms down. To call your mother when work slows. To repent after this phase. {trap}Far away is a comfortable place to keep things.{/trap} It quietly turns later into never.
old: There is plenty of time before any of this matters.
new: Thinking it is far away is exactly how people end up unready.
try: Pick one thing you keep saying you will do later. Do the first small step today.

title: But We see it near.
subtitle: Allah's view of time versus ours
then: Right after their view comes Allah's. Ibn Kathir notes that believers held its coming to be near, {idea}even though no one knows its time except Allah.{/idea} {idea}Whatever is approaching is near{/idea}, and it will surely happen.
now: Your phone says your next birthday is months away. Then it arrives, and the last year feels like a week. Every deadline you ever had felt far until it did not. {idea}Near is the honest word.{/idea}
old: The end is so far away it hardly affects my choices today.
new: Anything certain to come is already close.
try: Tonight, spend two minutes thinking: if it were near, what would I change first?

title: The sky will look like murky oil.
subtitle: The ceiling of the world melting
then: The surah now describes the Day the deniers mocked. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and others said the sky will be {trap}like the residue of oil.{/trap} The most stable thing anyone in Makkah could point to would lose its form.
now: You look up from the bus stop and the sky is just there, like it always has been. You build your life assuming the backdrop stays fixed. {idea}Even the backdrop has an end date.{/idea}
old: Some things in this world are permanent.
new: Nothing here is fixed. Even the sky will change.
try: Look up at the sky once today and remember it will not always look like this.

title: Mountains will float like fluffed wool.
subtitle: The heaviest things made light
then: Mujahid, Qatadah and As-Suddi said the mountains will be {trap}like fluffed wool{/trap}, as another verse calls it carded wool. For people who lived among the mountains of Makkah, nothing seemed more permanent.
now: The house you are paying off. The career you built for fifteen years. The body you trust to carry you. They feel like mountains. {idea}They are real, and they are not forever.{/idea}
old: The big, solid parts of my life will always hold me up.
new: Even mountains drift on that Day. Only what I did for Allah stays.
try: Name one solid thing you lean on. Thank Allah for it out loud.

title: No close friend will ask about a friend.
subtitle: When everyone is consumed with themselves

row.title: they are drowning too
sub: each has enough of his own

then: Ibn Kathir says no close friend will ask about his friend {trap}while he sees him in the worst of conditions.{/trap} He will be worried about himself. He links it to the verse: every man that Day will have enough to make him careless of others.
now: Think of the friend you call first in a crisis, the one in every family group chat who always replies. On that Day they will be facing their own record. {idea}The friendships worth having are the ones that help you prepare now.{/idea}
old: My people will have my back no matter what.
new: On that Day each person faces their own load. Help each other now, while it counts.
try: Send one friend a message today that reminds them of Allah, kindly.

title: He would hand over his own children to escape.
subtitle: The ransom no one expects to offer

row.title: I would die for my kids

then: They will be made to see one another, yet flee. Ibn Kathir says even the child {trap}dearer to him than the last beat of his heart{/trap} he would wish to offer as ransom when he sees the horrors. {trap}Even that would not be accepted.{/trap}
now: You hold your child at the school gate and feel you would give anything for them. That love is real. The verse shows how far terror on that Day goes. {idea}The best protection for your family is the faith you build with them today.{/idea}
old: Nothing could ever make me turn on the people I love.
new: That Day's fear is beyond anything I know. Preparing now is the real love.
try: Pray one prayer today with your family or child beside you.

title: His wife and his brother join the offer.
subtitle: The ransom list keeps growing
then: The list continues: his wife, then his brother. Ibn Kathir pairs this with the verse that {trap}a heavily laden soul calls another to carry its load{/trap}, and nothing is lifted, even by close kin.
now: Your brother covers for you with your parents. Your spouse handles the bills you forget. You lean on them for so much. {idea}On that Day, nobody can carry your deeds for you.{/idea}
old: My family will share whatever I end up facing.
new: Each person carries their own record. I should carry mine well.
try: Do one task today you usually leave for your spouse or sibling.

title: Even the clan that sheltered him.
subtitle: The tribe that always protected him
then: In Makkah the clan was everything. It protected you, fed you, avenged you. Mujahid and As-Suddi said fasilah means {idea}his tribe and his kin{/idea}. Ibn Kathir cites the verse that when the Trumpet is blown, {trap}there will be no kinship among them.{/trap}
now: Your surname opens doors. Your family's name gets you hired, forgiven, welcomed. That shelter is a gift. {trap}It does not carry over.{/trap} What carries over is how you used it.
old: Where I come from and who my family is will protect me.
new: The shelter of family ends at that Day. Only my deeds go further.
try: Use your family's name or connections today to help someone who has none.

title: He would give the whole earth to be saved.
subtitle: The biggest ransom imaginable
then: The offer reaches its limit. Ibn Kathir says {trap}no ransom will be accepted{/trap}, even if he brought all the people of the earth and enough gold to fill it. The deniers of Makkah trusted wealth. Here it is worth nothing.
now: Payday comes, and for a moment you feel secure. Insurance, savings, an emergency fund. These are wise here. {idea}None of it is currency on that Day.{/idea} The only thing that crosses is what you did.
old: With enough money, I can fix almost anything.
new: All the wealth of the earth cannot buy one soul out of that Day.
try: Give a small charity today, quietly, as a deposit for the Day.

title: No. It is the Flame.
subtitle: The bargaining is cut off
then: After all the offers, one word: {trap}No!{/trap} Ibn Kathir says Allah is describing the Fire and {trap}the severity of its heat.{/trap} The criminal's bargaining ends there. The time for making deals was in this life.
now: You have probably said it: I will sort it out with Allah later. As if there will be a meeting where you can explain. {idea}The meeting is now.{/idea} Every prayer, every apology, every time you turn back is the negotiation.
old: When the time comes, I will find a way to make things right.
new: The way to make things right is open today, and only today is promised.
try: Make one sincere istighfar today for a specific thing, naming it to Allah.
